## Design

### 2026-10-05 – I wanted to make an AI assistant using XiaoZhi AI, a free ai service for Esp32 boards.

**4h**

I wanted to make an AI assistant using XiaoZhi AI, a free ai service for Esp32 boards.

I chose an Esp32-S3 N16R8 for this project, as it was the most powerful one I had. I also grabbed a microphone module, a SPI display, and a Max amplifier.

The amplifier had the pins upside down for some reason, probably my fault when I got it a year or two ago, so I had to painstakingly remove all the solder and resolder it, and I had used crappy solder back then, so it was a pain to remove. I spent like a good 30 minutes trying to fix it. I eventually finished.

![image7](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/YbYkCwHwTjFG9wC6xdvuI01hSDybHHIh/8a82d7e601576e382b26c9f0097aa7c0bac1eb4fbeee7652e37c7305757a35c6.jpeg)

After that, I researched wiring diagrams for a good amount of time, and wired up the breadboard, which again was annoying because I bought crappy breadboard wires and didn't have a second breadboard to fit the whole Esp32 on it.

![image6](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/YbYkCwHwTjFG9wC6xdvuI01hSDybHHIh/27b3d92c90a1af3f7ac28358687c0825ed77e0b5eed28e532967cf3d83288f6f.jpeg)

After making probably the worst ever breadboard design, I started to flash the firmware onto the board.

First, I had to look up and download the flashing tool and the firmware. I spent like 20 minutes struggling with it before I realized I needed to unzip the firmware and upload what was INSIDE of the zip file.  After that fiaso, I again spent a good amount of time on trying to fix it, because it still wasnt working, and I realized I also had the wrong firmware too! After that, I finally got the screen to turn on with the XiaoZhi startup screen.

![image3 1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/YbYkCwHwTjFG9wC6xdvuI01hSDybHHIh/75b9136bd5f5717951cb8dd5f634d024a4ce3ab4fb5645ddd1dc65b86d8ecc22.jpeg)

I then connected to the boards wifi, then connected it to my local wifi, giving me access to change its settings. I had to wait a lil for a code which I could then put into the xiaozhi.me website, and I could configure a agent for it.

The problem is, the speaker isn't working. I can see on the console that its relaying ideas, but I think that the speaker and possibly the microphone don't work or are broken.

![image2 1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/YbYkCwHwTjFG9wC6xdvuI01hSDybHHIh/be35166655ee1dc9169be3b09f66f15a69f42c9f92ad9c570cd692955a00dfea.jpeg)

I ran out of time to do stuff today, but I'm pretty happy with how much I got done today! I think the next step after fixing the speaker and mic is to put it on a protoboard, then eventually a PCB!

### 2026-10-06 – Spent some time troubleshooting the issues with the screen (not showing any text), the mic (bad speech recognition), and speaker (no audio).

**2.5h**

Spent some time troubleshooting the issues with the screen (not showing any text), the mic (bad speech recognition), and speaker (no audio).

For the screen, I realized I again had a bad firmware, and I should have actually been using the Xiao Zhi firmware builder, so I customized it to fit my board and screen, which also allowed me to add a custom wake word and custom emojis. I of course, immediately made all the emojis just memes of iron man, because why not? I also made the wake word "Jarvis".

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/YbYkCwHwTjFG9wC6xdvuI01hSDybHHIh/9a106c99a5d50f3308424a92d9cfd1a48e54b983ab2a632ddac9e44d0fac0128.png)

![image2 2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/YbYkCwHwTjFG9wC6xdvuI01hSDybHHIh/2d73048bbf0e1ebbec5b5fdb8da4606c74b7d76aeda7859004b283fa7a1004f5.jpeg)

After that, I messed with the microphone, when I realized that I'm just an idiot who was too close to the mic, so I backed up and it works like a charm.

![image4 1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/YbYkCwHwTjFG9wC6xdvuI01hSDybHHIh/7c961af24a1258fca559fa5745346278d4b9922d4bca3fc2e412495ede7cd76b.jpeg)

The last problem was the audio. I spent a crazy amount of time troubleshooting it, I used a multimeter to check if it was getting  the right voltage, I triple checked the wiring, and I even swapped out the speaker, still nothing. The chatbot also said that it detected nothing wrong with the speaker, so I was at a loss. I have decided to suck it up and buy a new amplifier, and at the same time a better, louder speaker, because I was using a crappy tiny one. Will update when the new stuff arrives and I add it.

![image0 3](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/YbYkCwHwTjFG9wC6xdvuI01hSDybHHIh/b883c1900f5f749f1cfc524c03f9b8f4820c8a7931d8d8e0aa7e82487b6eb047.jpeg)

### 2026-10-06 – Small update today. I’m currently not at home, but I have done some extensive research on the capabilities of my XiaoZhi AI chatbot.

**2h**

Small update today. I’m currently not at home, but I have done some extensive research on the capabilities of my XiaoZhi AI chatbot.

For starters, I can program different functionalities such as turning on lights using MCP endpoints, by connecting things to GPIO pins and adding a small bit of code to it. So I can say, “Jarvis, turn on the lights”, and it will turn on a LED.

![IMG_4103](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/YbYkCwHwTjFG9wC6xdvuI01hSDybHHIh/6433e68c8e7ecc2da33dbfc4274ef3bd220d7ef0dc9bbfcbb7780aee1f2df439.png)

Another thing I have realized, is that some functionalities are locked behind a home server. Now this isn’t just a regular, self hosting AI server, but kinda a midpoint between the XiaoZhi servers and my chatbot. So basically, I can have more customization without a heavy LLM running on my spare laptop.

Some functionalities I can do with this is things like a custom tts voice, which I’m totally going to do with a Jarvis voice and I will literally have Jarvis at home. Another thing is real time internet searching, right now, it’s got a lot of knowledge, but narrow questions can’t be answered, as it can’t access the internet.

![IMG_4102](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/YbYkCwHwTjFG9wC6xdvuI01hSDybHHIh/5bbc8bc22ae0295ebe086998e0634e7f4bcf7ba34f564b5a7b32953518459551.jpeg)
Another cool thing to think about is giving it its own media library, such as song files, making it its own little Alexa player, with no ads for Amazon Music plus! Great for my little collection of mp3 files. With this library, it will also have a better memory, so it will be able to remember things from way back in time.

I think the main things I will be working on for now is mainly software related, planning out exactly what functions I want it to have, then going to making a PCB, where I will eventually make it a 3d case for the next series of things. Also can someone tell me how the weeks work, is it an actual physical week? Asking bc I’m going to San Francisco for the next few days and I don’t want to be left behind.

### 2026-10-07 – PCB TIME!!!

**3.5h**

PCB TIME!!!

I basically just took my wiring diagram from my breadboard and put it into EasyEDA. It took a little while to find some of the parts I needed, had to scour the user generated library, but I eventually found them all! Now we don't talk about aesthetics for my schematic...

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/YbYkCwHwTjFG9wC6xdvuI01hSDybHHIh/d3eb59ae3119463de85d483166811652131c47b6ff8cf5e70487a0a7caa5d04b.png)

Yeah it's basically unreadable, BUT IT WORKS OK!!! (I think)

I next started working on the design for the actual thing, and after some very professionaly sketching, I came up with this design for the finished assistant. It will have the main screen in the middle of the box, having the speaker at the very bottom and the microphone at the very top, to make sure there is no interference or anything. I put the esp32 and audio amp on the back of the pcb, as to make sure to keep the front side clear for the screen. I'm going to have an extension of the esp32's usb-c port on the back of the case, so I can power it and upload new firmware if I want to, along with having an extension of the boot and reset buttons on the back as well.

![image0 5](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/YbYkCwHwTjFG9wC6xdvuI01hSDybHHIh/6c29e04d7be9c3e52d179f26a1c2e25cf7ab15872dee80baeee4f35c8ec3a8b7.jpg)

Then I just adapted that to the PCB design!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/YbYkCwHwTjFG9wC6xdvuI01hSDybHHIh/8cc82f331f7ebefbeb6945b0d7feaef6e01b5663c58e3742957a321e17fbce02.png)

It took a little while to get the 3d models on the board, as most user generated footprints don't have 3d models, so I had to download some models off the internet to put on the footprints, but I think it turned out great!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/YbYkCwHwTjFG9wC6xdvuI01hSDybHHIh/fd97ba80a393793e6684c48c6ecc65e75968c814d03e14775bf5b3c138b3981c.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/YbYkCwHwTjFG9wC6xdvuI01hSDybHHIh/6532ad72137fefbcea4aa336455f6d9205a009b060ab1903e8f0043487dc6b2e.png)

The final thing I've been doing today is making the repository on github, I uploaded everything to the github, but for some reason the thing won't recognize my pcb files, I spent a whole lot of time trying to fix this, but no matter what I do, it won't recognize this. This is my last day before I leave to go to San Francisco, so I really hope someone can help me out with this, because I've really spent a lot of time on this and I don't want it all to be for naught.
